Hip and Thigh Pain and Numbness

groin vs lateral vs buttock · tendon vs nerve · which nerves have motor fibers · when to imageWhere is the pain, and is there tenderness, weakness or only numbness?

1Presentation2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Presentation
Bottom line
  • Sort by place: the groin is the joint; the lateral hip is the gluteal tendons or a sensory nerve; the buttock is the spine, the sacroiliac joint or the piriformis
  • Point tenderness over the greater trochanter, worse lying on that side, with a normal neurologic exam is greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS), however burning the pain sounds
  • A numb upper lateral thigh with full strength is meralgia paresthetica: the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve carries no motor fibers, so the diagnosis is clinical Sensory-only nervesLateral femoral cutaneous: anterior and lateral thigh. Saphenous (from the femoral nerve): medial leg. Sural: posterior lateral leg. A digital nerve between the third and fourth metatarsal heads: Morton neuroma, pain and a click when the heads are squeezed.
What it is

Pain or numbness around the hip and thigh in an adult: the joint, a tendon, or a nerve

Sort by

Where it hurts, then tenderness, weakness, or numbness alone

Hands off

A fall with a shortened, turned-out leg: Hip Injury in an Adult; back pain with sciatica: Low Back Pain in an Adult; treating hip osteoarthritis: Osteoarthritis

2Urgent risks
Femoral neck stress fractureRunner or recruit with groin pain on hopping; the radiograph is normal early

If groin pain follows overuse and the film is normal, choose MRI now; if missed, it can become a complete fracture.

Osteonecrosis of the femoral headGlucocorticoids, alcohol or sickle cell disease; groin pain on weight bearing; motion limited

If a risk factor comes with a normal film, choose MRI.

3Differential
Hip and thigh pain, most tempting first
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (trochanteric bursitis)Most often a woman aged 40 to 60; lateral hip pain lying on it, walking, or after long sittingTypically no inciting injury; point tenderness over the trochanter; no groin pain
Gluteus medius tendon tearLateral hip pain, weak abduction, Trendelenburg gaitGTPS still failing after an injection, or weak abduction: MRI or ultrasound
Hip osteoarthritisOlder; groin pain into the thigh or kneeTypically gradual onset; internal rotation painful and reduced; crepitus; stiffness under 30 minutes; radiograph
Femoral neck stress fractureRunner, possibly with energy imbalance (female athlete triad)Overuse in training; groin pain on hopping; MRI
Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (avascular necrosis)Glucocorticoids, alcohol, sickle cell diseaseProgressive groin pain, motion limited; no fever; MRI
Labral tearActive; clicking, catching or lockingFABER (flexion, abduction, external rotation) painful; MRI
Piriformis syndromeButtock pain down the back of the thigh, worse sittingDeep buttock tenderness; normal neurologic exam
Osteoid osteomaMale under 25; femoral pain at nightRelieved by an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug); a small lucent nidus
Iliotibial band syndromeRunner or cyclist; lateral knee painTender at the lateral femoral epicondyle: a knee diagnosis
Numbness or weakness: which nerve
DiagnosisFingerprintDecides it
Meralgia parestheticaBurning patch on the upper lateral thigh; tight belt, obesity, pregnancy, diabetesSensory only; strength and reflexes normal; no testing; loosen tight clothing
L2 to L3 radiculopathyBack pain into the anterior thigh; weak hip flexionPatellar reflex reduced, with back pain
Femoral neuropathyAnterior thigh and medial leg numbness after a pelvic fracture or a retroperitoneal hematomaWeak knee extension and hip flexion; patellar reflex reduced
Diabetic amyotrophyDiabetes; severe thigh pain and weight lossAsymmetric proximal weakness and wasting
4Workup
GTPS: start on the lowest rung not yet tried
RungDoMove on when
1Activity change, an NSAID, physical therapySymptoms persist
2Glucocorticoid injection at the trochanterStill failing, or weak abduction at any rung: MRI for a tear
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext best step
Years of metformin, numb feetVitamin B12 deficiency: a distal symmetric neuropathyCheck vitamin B12; a one-sided thigh patch is not this
Foot drop after habitual leg crossing or weight lossPeroneal palsy at the fibular neckTest hip abduction: weakness favors L5 radiculopathy
Lateral hip pain with a leg-length differenceGTPS, often from an overworked gluteus mediusActivity change, an NSAID and physical therapy, as for GTPS

Pause point. The bait: trusting the word "burning." Lateral tenderness with a normal neurologic exam is a tendon; numbness with full strength is a sensory nerve.

Practice
  1. 54-year-old woman has 3 months of lateral hip pain she calls burning worse lying on that side and on stairs point tenderness over the bony lateral hip Hip range of motion full; neurologic exam normal Afebrile · body mass index 33 → Greater trochanteric pain syndrome → tenderness over the trochanter with a normal neurologic exam outweighs the word burning: greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS); activity modification, an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) and physical therapy
  2. 58-year-old woman was diagnosed with greater trochanteric pain syndrome 2 months ago still tender over the trochanter 8 weeks of an NSAID and abductor-strengthening therapy No weakness or limp Afebrile · hip range of motion full → Corticosteroid injection → refractory to an NSAID and physical therapy: corticosteroid injection; MRI is for suspected tendon tear
  3. 66-year-old woman has 6 months of lateral hip pain weak hip abduction Trendelenburg gait Tender over the greater trochanter; worse lying on that side Afebrile · no back pain · sensation and reflexes normal · hip internal rotation full → Gluteus medius tendon tear → abductor weakness with a Trendelenburg gait is the severe end of the GTPS spectrum, a gluteus medius tendon tear: MRI; weakness separates a tear from uncomplicated GTPS, which has normal strength
  4. 67-year-old man has 2 years of groin pain pain radiates to the knee, worse after walking internal rotation reduced, with crepitus Morning stiffness under 30 minutes Afebrile · body mass index 29 · no trochanteric tenderness → Hip OA → groin pain with reduced internal rotation and crepitus is the joint itself, hip osteoarthritis: radiograph
  5. 26-year-old woman training for a marathon has groin pain pain when she hops on that leg log-roll of the leg reproduces the groin pain Hip radiograph normal; irregular periods Afebrile · body mass index 18 → Femoral neck stress fracture → groin pain on hopping in a runner with a normal film is a femoral neck stress fracture: MRI; irregular periods and low weight suggest the female athlete triad
  6. 30-year-old man, a cyclist, has lateral knee pain tender over the lateral femoral condyle Noble test reproduces it Hip examination normal; rides 200 km a week Afebrile · BP 118/70 mm Hg · no knee effusion → IT band syndrome → lateral knee pain at the femoral condyle with a positive Noble test is iliotibial (IT) band syndrome, a knee diagnosis, not a hip one
  7. 40-year-old man has numbness over the upper lateral thigh a patch that burns when he wears a tight belt no tenderness over the trochanter; no back pain Strength normal; reflexes normal Afebrile · body mass index 36 → Meralgia paresthetica → a sensory-only patch on the upper lateral thigh with normal strength is meralgia paresthetica; a radiculopathy usually brings back pain, a dermatomal pattern or weakness
  8. 16-year-old boy has 3 months of thigh pain pain wakes him at night ibuprofen relieves it dramatically No trauma; no weight loss Afebrile · radiograph: small lucency with sclerosis in the proximal femur → Osteoid osteoma → night pain dramatically relieved by NSAIDs in a young patient is an osteoid osteoma; CT (computed tomography) shows the nidus
  9. 45-year-old man on prednisone for 2 years has progressive groin pain drinks heavily range of motion reduced in all planes Hip radiograph normal; no trauma Afebrile · BP 124/78 mm Hg · hemoglobin normal → AVN → steroids or alcohol with groin pain and a normal film is avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral head: MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)
  10. 38-year-old woman has 2 months of right buttock pain pain runs down the back of the thigh worse sitting, tender deep in the buttock No back pain; straight-leg raise negative Afebrile · strength, reflexes and sensation normal → Piriformis syndrome → buttock pain sorts to the spine, sacroiliac joint or piriformis; worse sitting with piriformis tenderness and a normal neurologic exam fits piriformis syndrome
  11. 44-year-old man, obese, has burning numbness over the upper lateral thigh wears a tight work belt every day no back pain Strength 5/5 throughout Afebrile · BP 136/86 mm Hg · reflexes normal · body mass index 37 → Meralgia paresthetica → the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve is purely sensory, so full strength confirms meralgia paresthetica: weight loss and loosening restrictive belts
  12. 44-year-old man has numbness over the anterior thigh and medial leg weak knee extension reduced patellar reflex Began after a long procedure in the lithotomy position; no back pain Afebrile · BP 128/80 mm Hg → Femoral neuropathy → anterior thigh and medial leg numbness with quadriceps weakness and a reduced patellar reflex is a femoral neuropathy
  13. 44-year-old man has 2 months of lateral thigh numbness back pain radiating to the knee reduced patellar reflex, weak hip flexion Femoral stretch test positive; no bladder symptoms Afebrile · BP 132/84 mm Hg → L2–L3 radiculopathy → back pain with weakness, a reduced reflex and a positive femoral stretch test is an L2 to L3 radiculopathy; meralgia has no motor or reflex loss
  14. 56-year-old woman has 2 months of lateral hip pain point tenderness over the bony lateral hip no numbness Worse lying on that side and climbing stairs Afebrile · strength normal · knee examination normal → Trochanteric bursitis → trochanteric tenderness without numbness is trochanteric bursitis, the older, misnamed label for greater trochanteric pain syndrome; the exam may still use it
  15. 60-year-old man with diabetes has severe right thigh pain proximal leg weakness and thigh wasting lost 7 kg in 2 months Asymmetric; the left leg is spared Afebrile · hemoglobin A1c 9.1% → Diabetic amyotrophy → severe asymmetric thigh pain, proximal weakness and weight loss in diabetes is diabetic amyotrophy; polyneuropathy is symmetric and starts in the feet
  16. 44-year-old man has burning numbness over the upper lateral thigh since he started wearing a tool belt strength and reflexes normal No back pain Afebrile · sensory loss in a patch on the upper lateral thigh → No testing; it is a clinical diagnosis → meralgia paresthetica is a clinical diagnosis; no imaging or electrodiagnostic testing is needed
Transferable rule

When the pain quality and the findings disagree, rely on the findings. A nerve's motor content sets what its lesion can look like: if it has no motor fibers, a normal motor exam confirms rather than refutes.
